mainTopic: A חרש's mind and his גט; divorcing a שוטה wife; רבי יוחנן בן נורי's challenge; a גט called a loan document
overview: The amud opens by finishing רב אשי's question about a חרש. Is his mind weak but steady every day, or does it switch between clear and unclear? The difference is whether he can give his wife a גט, and the question ends in תיקו. Next the גמרא turns to a wife who became a שוטה. רבי יצחק says that by Torah law she could be divorced, but the רבנן forbade it so people would not treat her as הפקר. After challenges from the schools of רבי ינאי and רבי ישמעאל, the גמרא sets the case: she understands her גט but cannot protect herself. אביי supports this from the משנה's use of the word 'never' only for the husband. The גמרא then shows that רבי יוחנן בן נורי was challenging the רבנן on their own terms. רבא learns from רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא that a גט handed over as a 'loan document' still divorces. The amud ends with the start of a story about keys lost on שבת, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First possibility: a weak mind that never changes
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי's question continues. Maybe רבי אלעזר is unsure whether a חרש's mind is clear, while being sure that his mind is always at the same level.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe his mind is not clear, but he is always of one steady mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the first side of רב אשי's question about what makes רבי אלעזר unsure about a חרש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this side, the doubt is about the quality of the חרש's mind: is it clear or not? What is not in doubt is that his mind stays the same from day to day. It does not switch back and forth.

keyTerms.meaning: a deaf-mute, treated in הלכה as having limited understanding

phrases.english: or if his mind is not clear,
but he is always of one mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the first side of רב אשי's question, which began before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רבי אלעזר's doubt only about whether the חרש's steady mind counts as clear?

steps.title: Second possibility: a mind that goes back and forth
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe רבי אלעזר is sure that a חרש's mind is weak. His doubt comes from the fact that the חרש is sometimes healthy and sometimes a שוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe it is obvious to him that his mind is weak and not clear. Here the reason for the doubt is that sometimes he is healthy and sometimes he is a שוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of רב אשי's question: a different reason for רבי אלעזר's doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the weakness of the mind is taken as certain. The doubt comes from instability: on any given day we do not know which state he is in. So the doubt is about timing, not about the quality of his mind.

keyTerms.meaning: or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that something is doubtful. The question is what is doubtful: the quality of his mind, or whether it is steady.

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is obvious to him
that his mind is weak
and it is not a clear mind,
and here, this is the reason:
since at times he is healthy and at times imbecilic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the other side of the question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רבי אלעזר's doubt caused by the חרש switching between clear and unclear states?

steps.title: What difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the practical difference between the two possibilities.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why it matters which side is true. It is setting up the next step, where it will show a real case that depends on the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides lead to the same result for תרומה. So the גמרא looks for a case where the two explanations would actually give different rulings.

phrases.english: For what is there a practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the two-sided question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two explanations would give different rulings.

steps.title: The difference: can a חרש divorce his wife?
steps.stepSummary: If his mind is steady, his גירושין match his קידושין, so he can divorce. If his mind goes back and forth, he can marry but cannot divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is whether he can divorce his wife with a גט. If you say he has one steady mind, then just as his קידושין works, so does his גירושין. If you say he is sometimes healthy and sometimes a שוטה, he can marry but he cannot divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference shows up when a חרש wants to give his wife a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a steady mind, he is at the same level when he divorces as when he married, so the גט matches the קידושין. With a mind that switches, he may have married on a clear day and now be unclear. So we let the marriage stand, but we do not let him divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: as with the betrothal, so with the divorce

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a mind that switches back and forth causes a lopsided result: strictness pushes us to keep the marriage and to block the divorce.

phrases.english: To send out his wife with a bill of divorce.
If you say he is of one mind,
as is the betrothal, so is the divorce.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ עִתִּים חָלִים וְעִתִּים שׁוֹטֶה —
phrases.english: But if you say at times he is healthy and at times imbecilic,
he can betroth,
but he cannot divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the practical difference.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is whether a חרש can divorce his wife: yes if his mind is steady, no if it switches back and forth.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which side is true and leaves it as תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the answer? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot decide between the two possibilities, so it closes this question with תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No proof is found for either side. Because of that, the question of whether a חרש can give a גט stays in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand: the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's question (a weak but steady mind, or a mind that switches back and forth) was never answered, so a חרש's ability to divorce stays in doubt.

phrases.english: What is it? Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question about רבי אלעזר's reasoning remains unresolved (תיקו).

steps.title: By Torah law, a שוטה wife can be divorced
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's case of a wife who became a שוטה, רבי יצחק says that by Torah law she could be divorced, just as a competent woman can be divorced against her will.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the משנה's words 'she became a שוטה': רבי יצחק said that by Torah law a שוטה can be divorced, just like a competent woman who is divorced against her will.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה and brings רבי יצחק's teaching about a wife who lost her sanity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman's agreement is not needed for a גט. So her losing her sanity should not, by Torah law, stop the divorce. It works the same way as divorcing a healthy woman against her will.

keyTerms.meaning: she became a שוטה (lost her sanity)

phrases.english: "She became imbecilic," etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: a man whose wife became a שוטה may not divorce her.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
By Torah law, an imbecilic woman can be divorced,
just as it is with a competent woman against her will.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, based on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By Torah law, a שוטה wife can be divorced, since a woman's agreement is not needed.

steps.title: So why did the רבנן say she cannot be divorced?
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah allows it, why does the משנה rule that she cannot be divorced?
steps.simpleTranslation: So what is the reason they said she is not divorced?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק goes on to ask why the משנה forbids the divorce if Torah law allows it. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק has just shown that the Torah does not block the divorce. So the משנה's ruling must be a rule of the רבנן, and he now gives its reason.

keyTerms.meaning: and what is the reason they said

phrases.english: And what is the reason they said she is not divorced?
phrases.notes: 'They' means the רבנן of the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the משנה's ruling, given רבי יצחק's teaching.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the רבנן forbade divorcing a שוטה wife.

steps.title: To protect her from being treated as ownerless
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן blocked the divorce so that people would not take advantage of her as if she were הפקר.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that people should not treat her like ownerless property.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק explains that the רבנן's rule is meant to protect the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a husband to look after her, and without her own good judgment, people might abuse her. Keeping her married gives her protection, even though the Torah itself would allow the divorce.
steps.whatToRemember: A שוטה wife can be divorced by Torah law, but the רבנן forbade it to protect her from being treated as הפקר.

phrases.english: So that they should not treat her in the manner of ownerless property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the reason for the רבנן's ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling protects her from being exploited as if she were ownerless.

steps.title: What kind of שוטה are we talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exact case the משנה means. It rules out a woman who can protect both her גט and herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If she knows how to guard her גט and how to guard herself, would anyone treat her as ownerless?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to pin down exactly which woman the משנה and רבי יצחק are talking about. It first tries one possibility and rejects it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason the רבנן gave was that people would treat her like הפקר. A woman who can take care of herself would never be treated that way. So she cannot be the case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact circumstances?
If you say (a suggestion about to be tested)
To guard her גט, meaning she understands what a divorce document is
Treating someone as ownerless, taking advantage of her

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say that she knows how to guard her bill of divorce
and she knows how to take care of herself
would people treat her as ownerless?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which woman fits the reason given in step 8, that the רבנן blocked the divorce because of הפקר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which level of mental impairment the משנה and רבי יצחק are describing.

steps.title: First answer: she can guard neither her גט nor herself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the case is a woman who understands neither her גט nor how to protect herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must be a woman who knows how to guard neither her גט nor herself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer about which woman the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a fully capable woman does not fit, the גמרא jumps to the other extreme: a woman with no understanding at all. This answer is about to be challenged in the next step.

phrases.english: Rather, where she does not know how to guard
either her bill of divorce or herself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, דְּאֵין יוֹדַעַת לִשְׁמוֹר לֹא גִּיטָּהּ וְלֹא עַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 after ruling out the capable woman.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is a woman who understands neither her גט nor how to protect herself.

steps.title: Challenge from the school of רבי ינאי: she needs a 'hand'
steps.stepSummary: If she understands nothing, how can רבי יצחק say the Torah allows her divorce? The school of רבי ינאי learns from the פסוק that a woman without understanding cannot be divorced at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can a שוטה really be divorced by Torah law? But the school of רבי ינאי said: 'and he shall give it into her hand' means a woman who has a 'hand' to receive her own divorce. This excludes a woman who has no such 'hand'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 10. It quotes a teaching showing that a woman with no understanding cannot be divorced even by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק said that by Torah law this woman could be divorced. But if she understands nothing, the Torah itself disqualifies her, because the פסוק requires a woman who can take the גט into her own 'hand'. So either step 10's case or רבי יצחק's ruling must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law, as opposed to a rule of the רבנן
'Hand': here, the mental ability to receive a גט

phrases.english: Can a שוטה really be divorced by Torah law?
But the school of Rabbi Yannai said:
"And he shall give it into her hand"

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ יָד לְגָרֵשׁ עַצְמָהּ
phrases.english: this means one who has a 'hand' to receive her own divorce
phrases.notes: 'Hand' here means she has enough understanding to accept the גט herself.

phrases.english: this excludes this woman
who has no 'hand' to receive her own divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה שׁוֹטָה מִתְגָּרֶשֶׁת? וְהָא אָמַר דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 10's answer, because that woman could not be divorced even by Torah law.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 10's case, read together with רבי יצחק's claim that a שוטה can be divorced by Torah law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק 'ונתן בידה' requires a woman able to receive the גט. A woman with no understanding is excluded by the Torah itself.

steps.title: A second source from the school of רבי ישמעאל: she must not come back
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל learns the same thing from 'and send her from his house'. A divorce works only for a woman who, once sent away, does not come back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'and he sends her from his house' means a woman he sends away who does not return. This excludes a woman he sends away who comes right back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second teaching that supports the challenge of step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a different reading of the next words of the same פסוק. A woman who does not understand divorce will simply walk back into the house, so the divorce does not really 'send her away'. Again, the Torah would not allow her divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught
'And he sends her from his house' (part of the פסוק about divorce)

phrases.english: And the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"And he sends her out of his house"
this means one whom he sends away and she does not return
this excludes this woman
whom he sends away and she comes back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of step 11 with a second teaching.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge that a woman with no understanding cannot be divorced by Torah law
steps.raayaSupportSource: The school of רבי ישמעאל's reading of 'ושלחה מביתו'

steps.title: The real case: she understands her גט but cannot protect herself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the case to a woman who understands her גט but cannot take care of herself. By Torah law she can be divorced, but the רבנן blocked it so people would not treat her as הפקר.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the case is needed for a woman who knows how to guard her גט but does not know how to guard herself. By Torah law she can be divorced, since she understands her גט. But the רבנן said he should not divorce her, so that people will not treat her as ownerless.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to a middle case. This woman is impaired, but not so badly that the Torah disqualifies her divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because she understands her גט, she has a 'hand' and will not come back, so the Torah teachings of steps 11 and 12 do not exclude her. Because she cannot protect herself, the הפקר worry is real. That is why the רבנן stepped in. This replaces the answer of step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for a specific case
The Sages, who can add protective rules beyond Torah law

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's שוטה understands her גט but cannot protect herself. By Torah law she can be divorced, but the רבנן forbade it so that no one would take advantage of her.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't hold on to the answer of step 10. The גמרא dropped it, because a woman who understands nothing could not be divorced even by Torah law.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a clear line. Understanding the גט is what the Torah requires for divorce. Being able to protect herself is the extra concern the רבנן added.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
for a woman who knows how to guard her bill of divorce
but does not know how to take care of herself.
By Torah law this שוטה can be divorced
since she knows how to guard her bill of divorce.
But the רבנן said he should not divorce her
so that people will not treat her as ownerless.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּיוֹדַעַת לִשְׁמוֹר גִּיטָּהּ וְאֵינָהּ יוֹדַעַת לִשְׁמוֹר עַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of steps 11 and 12 by defining a middle case that replaces step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's case was a woman with no understanding at all, and such a woman cannot be divorced even by Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is a woman who understands her גט but cannot protect herself. The Torah allows her divorce, and the רבנן forbade it to protect her.

steps.title: אביי shows the משנה's wording supports the answer
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that the משנה uses the word 'never' only for the insane husband. This shows his case is דאורייתא and the insane wife's case is דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The wording of the משנה also shows this. About the wife it says, 'If she became insane, he may not divorce her.' About the husband it says, 'He may never divorce.' Why add 'never' in one place and not the other? It must be that the husband's rule is from the Torah and the wife's rule is from the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings support from the exact words of the משנה for the answer in step 13: divorcing an insane wife is blocked only by the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'never' about an insane husband but not about an insane wife. אביי reads the extra word 'never' as marking the stronger, Torah-level ban. Leaving it out for the wife shows that her rule is only from the רבנן, which fits step 13's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also precise: the exact wording supports this

steps.whatToRemember: Insane husband: he can never divorce, by Torah law. Insane wife who still understands her גט: the רבנן block the divorce, so the משנה does not say 'never.'

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is also precise,
for it teaches regarding her,
"if she became insane, he may not divorce her,"
and regarding him
phrases.notes: 'Him' means the husband who himself became insane.

phrases.english: "he may never divorce."
What is different here, that it teaches "never,"
and what is different there, that it does not teach "never"?
Rather, learn from it:
this one is from the Torah,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the insane husband, who can't give a גט.

phrases.english: that one is rabbinic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 13's answer from the משנה's wording.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the insane wife's case is only דרבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה uses 'עולמית' for the husband but not for the wife.

steps.title: What was רבי יוחנן בן נורי puzzled about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוחנן בן נורי's question from the משנה. It asks which side was clear to him: the deaf man or the deaf woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'רבי יוחנן בן נורי said...' The scholars asked: Was the man's case obvious to רבי יוחנן בן נורי, so he was asking about the woman? Or was the woman's case obvious to him, so he was asking about the man?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It asks what exactly רבי יוחנן בן נורי found hard to understand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה he asked why a wife who became a חרשת can be divorced, while a husband who became a חרש cannot divorce. The גמרא wants to know which half he took for granted. It also wants to know which half seemed strange to him.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the scholars
This is what he is asking about

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: "Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said, etc."
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: why can a wife who became deaf be divorced, while a husband who became deaf can't divorce?

phrases.english: A question was asked:
Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri:
is the man obvious to him,
and he is asking about the woman?
Or perhaps:
the woman is obvious to him,
and he is asking about the man?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic on the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case, the deaf man or the deaf woman, was puzzling to רבי יוחנן בן נורי.

steps.title: The רבנן's reply suggests he was asking about the man
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answered by explaining why a man is different: a man divorces only by his own will. That suggests the man's case was the one in question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear. They told him: 'A man who divorces is not like a woman who is divorced. A woman can be divorced whether she wants it or not, but a man divorces only if he wants to.' Learn from this that he was asking about the man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from the way the רבנן responded to רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their answer focuses on the man needing his own will, which a חרש cannot properly show. If the answer explains the man, then the question must have been about the man.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who is divorced (the wife)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
from what they said to him:
The man who divorces is not similar
to the woman who is divorced,
for the woman goes out willingly or unwillingly,
and the man divorces only willingly;
learn from it that he was asking about the man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a proof for the second side of the question in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן בן נורי was puzzled about the man.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The רבנן's reply explaining why a man needs his own will.

steps.title: Another line of the reply suggests he was asking about the woman
steps.stepSummary: On the contrary: the רבנן also said 'this one too is like it.' That suggests the woman was the case in question.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! They also told him, 'This one too is like it.' Learn from this that he was asking about the woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It shows another phrase from the רבנן that points the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'This one too is like it' explains the woman's status. So the reply can be read as explaining either side. The proof from step 16 is therefore not decisive.

keyTerms.meaning: This one too is like it

phrases.english: On the contrary,
from what they said to him:
"This one too is like it"
learn from it that he was asking about the woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 16's proof with an opposite inference.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that he was asking about the man.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Another part of the רבנן's reply points to the woman, so the reply proves nothing.

steps.title: He was only challenging the רבנן on their own terms
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי himself held that neither a deaf man nor a deaf woman can be divorced. He was asking the רבנן how they could tell the two apart, and they answered him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן בן נורי spoke to them according to their own view. He said: 'In my view, just as a man cannot divorce, a woman also cannot be divorced. But in your view, what difference is there between a woman and a man?' They answered him: 'A man who divorces is not like a woman who is divorced.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question. Neither case was obvious to him. He held both are the same, and he was simply challenging the רבנן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his own view, a חרש cannot divorce and a חרשת cannot be divorced. His question was a challenge to the רבנן, who split the two cases. Their reply about the man's will was their defense of that split.

keyTerms.meaning: According to their own words or view

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן בן נורי treats a deaf husband and a deaf wife the same: no divorce in either case. The רבנן say the wife is different because a woman can be divorced even against her will.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבי יוחנן בן נורי's question as a sign that he agreed with the משנה's ruling. He disagreed with it. He was asking the רבנן to defend their own distinction.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri
was speaking to them according to their view:
According to me,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּאִישׁ לָא מָצֵי מְגָרֵשׁ
phrases.english: just as a man cannot divorce,
a woman also cannot be divorced;
but according to you,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא אִשָּׁה וּמַאי שְׁנָא אִישׁ!
phrases.english: what is different about a woman, and what is different about a man!
They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה הָאִישׁ הַמְגָרֵשׁ לָאִשָּׁה הַמִּתְגָּרֶשֶׁת.
phrases.english: The man who divorces is not similar to the woman who is divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי לְדִבְרֵיהֶם קָאָמַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question of step 15 after both proofs fell away.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Neither case was obvious to him. He held both cannot divorce and was challenging the רבנן's distinction.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן בן נורי: no divorce for a חרש or a חרשת. רבנן: a חרשת can be divorced because a woman's consent is not needed.

steps.title: רבא: A גט handed over as a 'loan document' still divorces
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא's testimony that if a husband tells witnesses he is giving a גט but tells his wife to take a שטר חוב, she is divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא testified. רבא said: from his testimony we learn this. If a man says to witnesses, "See this גט that I am giving," and says to his wife, "Take this loan document," she is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא's testimony. רבא then draws a practical rule from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the wife thinks she is receiving a loan document, not a גט. רבא says this does not matter: the divorce still works. The next step explains how he gets this from the testimony.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan testified, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא testified that a deaf girl married off by her father can be divorced.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: מֵעֵדוּתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן גּוּדְגְּדָא,
phrases.english: From the testimony of Rabbi Yochanan ben Gudgada we learn:
If a husband said to witnesses:
"See this get that I am giving,"
and he said to her: "Take this loan document,"
she is divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מֵעֵדוּתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן גּוּדְגְּדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יוחנן בן נורי's question in the משנה to the next part of the משנה, the testimony of רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wife who receives a גט she thinks is a שטר חוב is divorced, as long as the husband told the witnesses it was a גט.

steps.title: Why the testimony proves רבא's rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא holds that the wife's understanding is not required. So here too her understanding is not required.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא say that we don't need her understanding? Here too we don't need her understanding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבא's rule comes from the testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A deaf woman cannot understand that she is being divorced, yet רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא says she can be divorced. So her knowing is not needed. The same is true of a woman who thinks she is getting a loan document.

phrases.aramaic: מִי לָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן גּוּדְגְּדָא
phrases.english: Didn't Rabbi Yochanan ben Gudgada say
that we do not require her understanding?
Here too we do not require her understanding.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן גּוּדְגְּדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבא's rule in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That a wife's knowledge is not needed for a divorce, even when she thinks the document is a loan document.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא's testimony that a deaf woman can be divorced.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבא added, since it seems obvious from the testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא: if the testimony already shows that her understanding is not needed, why did he need to say anything?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule seems to follow simply from the testimony, so רבא's statement looks like it adds nothing new. The גמרא now has to find what is new in it.

phrases.english: Isn't it obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבא's rule from steps 19-20 adds anything new.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If her understanding is clearly not required, the rule is already obvious and needs no separate teaching.

steps.title: The real point: calling it a loan document does not cancel the גט
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought that saying "take this שטר חוב" cancels the גט. רבא teaches that it does not. A real cancellation would have been said to the witnesses. He said it to her only out of embarrassment.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since he told her "take this loan document," he canceled the גט. So רבא teaches us otherwise. If he had really canceled it, he would have told the witnesses. Since he did not tell the witnesses, he did not cancel it at all. He said this to her only because he was embarrassed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing what is new in רבא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is not about her understanding. It is about whether the husband's words cancel the גט. They do not: what counts is what he told the witnesses. His words to her were just a way to avoid an embarrassing moment.
steps.whatToRemember: A husband's words to his wife calling the גט a loan document do not cancel it. To cancel it, he would have to tell the witnesses.
steps.confusionAlert: The new point here is not that her understanding is unnecessary; that was already known. It is that his misleading words do not cancel the גט.

phrases.english: You might have said:
since he said to her, "Take this loan document,"
he fully canceled the get.
So רבא teaches us otherwise.
If it were true that he canceled it,
he would have said so to the witnesses.
And since he did not say it to the witnesses,
he did not cancel it at all.
And the fact that he said this
he said it only because of embarrassment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: identifies a reasonable mistake the rule prevents
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Calling the גט a loan document might have canceled it.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is not canceled, since he did not cancel it in front of the witnesses. His words to her came from embarrassment.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The גט is valid. Only a cancellation told to the witnesses would undo it.

steps.title: Story: keys to the study hall lost on Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins: רב יצחק בר ביסנא lost the keys of the בית מדרש in a רשות הרבים on שבת and went to ask רבי פדת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר ביסנא lost the keys of the בית מדרש in the public domain on שבת. He came before רבי פדת. רבי פדת said to him: Go...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new story. It is setting up a question about how to get into the בית מדרש on שבת, and רבי פדת's answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is that carrying keys in a רשות הרבים on שבת is forbidden. The story stops in the middle of רבי פדת's reply, so his advice comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: public domain, where carrying on שבת is forbidden

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Bisna
lost the keys of the study hall
in the public domain on Shabbat.
He came before Rabbi Pedat.
He said to him: Go...
phrases.notes: רבי פדת's instructions continue on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יִצְחָק בַּר בִּיסְנָא אִירְכַסוּ לֵיהּ מַפְתְּחֵי דְּבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unconnected to the divorce discussion just finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case of keys lost on שבת; the ruling follows on the next amud.
